title: 9 Best PostgreSQL Reporting Tools In 2026
summary: PostgreSQL reporting tools compared for 2026, from Metabase and Grafana to Power BI and GetDot, plus how to report on a production Postgres without hurting it.
body_markdown:
## How I compared them


Reports are long reads that compete with your application's transactions, so beyond price I looked at how each tool reaches a database in a private network (SSL, SSH tunnels, allowlists, gateways) and what it asks of the database user. Tool facts come from vendor docs and pricing pages, linked in each section; confirm prices before you budget. For thesafety section , we ran every step on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 instance with a streaming replica; the errors quoted are the ones it returned. Dot is our product, described from our public integration pages and changelog.


## 1. Metabase


**How it connects to Postgres:** directly. From Metabase Cloud, you allowlist Metabase's IP addresses and turn on SSL, or keep the database private behind an SSH tunnel to a bastion host ([Metabase's article on Cloud SQL connections](https://www.metabase.com/articles/metabase-vs-looker-studio) ). Its docs show the read-only pattern:` USAGE` on the schema and` SELECT` on its tables ([users, roles and privileges](https://www.metabase.com/docs/latest/databases/users-roles-privileges) ).


**Pricing:** beyond the table, extra users cost $6 (Starter) or $12 (Pro), yearly billing lowers the plans to $90 and $517.50 a month, and Enterprise starts at $20,000 a year ([Metabase pricing](https://www.metabase.com/pricing) ).


**Limits:** every Metabase query arrives as the one database user you configured, so give Metabase its own login to tell its queries apart in` pg_stat_activity` .


## 2. Grafana


**How it connects to Postgres:** the built-in PostgreSQL data source. Grafana's docs say the database user should have only` SELECT` on the schemas and tables you query, because Grafana does not check that queries are safe ([Grafana's PostgreSQL docs](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/datasources/postgres/configure/) ).


**Pricing:** open source and free to self-host. Grafana Cloud has a Free tier with usage limits, Pro from $19 a month plus usage, and Enterprise at a custom price with a $25,000 annual minimum commit ([Grafana pricing](https://grafana.com/pricing/) ).


**Limits:** business questions that aren't "this number over time" are easier in Metabase or Superset.


## 3. Apache Superset and Preset


**How it connects to Postgres:** a SQLAlchemy URI such as` postgresql://user:password@host:5432/dbname` ([Superset's database connection docs](https://superset.apache.org/user-docs/6.0.0/configuration/databases/) ). Preset is the managed version.


**Pricing:** Preset Starter is free for up to 5 users, Professional is $25 billed monthly, and Enterprise is custom ([Preset pricing](https://preset.io/pricing/) ).


**Limits:** self-hosting means you own upgrades, caching and authentication, and someone technical usually sets up datasets before business users can build charts.


## 4. Power BI


**How it connects to Postgres:** the Power Query PostgreSQL connector, in Import or DirectQuery mode, as a cloud connection or through an on-premises or virtual network data gateway for a database in a private network. Gateways released from June 2025 bundle the Npgsql provider; older ones need it installed separately ([Microsoft's PostgreSQL connector docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/connectors/postgresql) ).


**Pricing:** Pro is $14 per user per month and Premium Per User $24, both billed annually ([DashboardFox](https://dashboardfox.com/blog/real-cost-microsoft-power-bi/) ).


**Limits:** the gateway is one more server to keep updated. DirectQuery sends visuals' queries straight to your database, with a 4-minute timeout per query in the service ([DirectQuery guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/desktop-directquery-about) ); Import mode avoids that load but is only as fresh as the last refresh.


## 5. Tableau


**How it connects to Postgres:** the PostgreSQL connector with a Require SSL checkbox ([Tableau's PostgreSQL help](https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/examples_postgresql.htm) ). Tableau Cloud reaches an internet-facing database that allowlists it ([live connections](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/to_connect_live_sql.htm) ); for a private network, Tableau Bridge connects outbound with no inbound firewall changes ([Tableau Bridge docs](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/to_sync_local_data.htm) ).


**Pricing:** Standard edition Creator $75, Explorer $42 and Viewer $15 per user per month; Enterprise edition $115, $70 and $35; billed annually. These are third-party figures ([DashboardFox](https://dashboardfox.com/guides/bi-software-pricing-guide/tableau-pricing-explained/) ).


**Limits:** per-seat licensing adds up for people who only view, and Bridge is another agent to run for private databases.


## 6. Data Studio (formerly Looker Studio)


**How it connects to Postgres:** a native connector with an Enable SSL option, under constraints worth knowing before you start ([Data Studio's PostgreSQL docs](https://cloud.google.com/looker/docs/studio/connect-to-postgresql) ):


- A query returns at most 150,000 rows; anything beyond that is truncated.
- Private IP connections to Cloud SQL aren't supported, and the connector doesn't use the Cloud SQL proxy. You add Data Studio's IP ranges to the instance's authorized networks.
- Picking a table from the menu only works in the` public` schema; for other schemas you write a custom query.
- Column names must be ASCII.


**Pricing:** free; Data Studio Pro is $9 per user per project per month ([Data Studio](https://cloud.google.com/datastudio) ).


**Limits:** the public-IP requirement is the big one: many security teams will refuse to open a production database to Google's address ranges. See[Looker Studio alternatives](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/looker-studio-alternatives) for the usual next steps.


## 7. Retool and Appsmith (internal tools)


If the "report" is really a screen where support looks up a customer and changes something, you want an internal tool builder: Retool and Appsmith build tables, forms and buttons on Postgres that read and write.


**Pricing:** Retool's Team plan is $10 per builder per month plus $5 per internal user per month, billed annually, with higher Business and custom Enterprise tiers ([Retool pricing](https://retool.com/pricing) ). Appsmith's Community Edition is open source and free to self-host, and its Business plan is $15 per user per month (third-party figure,[Jet Admin's 2026 guide](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/appsmith-pricing-2026-guide-to-plans-limits-and-total-cost-with-jet-admin-comparison/) ).


**Limits:** they need write access, so give them their own role with only the writes they need, separate from your reporting role. They aren't built for open-ended questions.


## 8. Hex


**How it connects to Postgres:** directly, with Hex's static outbound IP addresses (they differ by region) on your allowlist, or through an SSH tunnel to a bastion host that Hex opens on demand, installing nothing in your network ([Hex's Postgres guide](https://learn.hex.tech/docs/connect-to-data/data-connections/setup-guides/connect-to-postgres) ,[SSH docs](https://learn.hex.tech/docs/connect-to-data/data-connections/connect-via-ssh) ).


**Pricing:** Community is free; Professional is $36 and Team $75 per editor per month; Enterprise is custom ([Hex pricing](https://hex.tech/pricing/) ).


**Limits:** Hex is a notebook first, so the people building need SQL or Python.


## 9. GetDot: answers and dashboards on Postgres in plain language


Dot answers questions about your Postgres data in Slack, Teams, email, the web app or an MCP client such as Claude, and shows the SQL it ran next to every answer.


**How it connects to Postgres:** a read-only user and group you create, SSL required by default, and an SSH tunnel through a bastion if the database is private. It works with RDS, Cloud SQL, Azure and self-hosted Postgres, on your app's database or its read replica ([Postgres integration](https://www.getdot.ai/integrations/postgres) ). On[Supabase](https://www.getdot.ai/integrations/supabase) it connects through the session pooler and skips Supabase's system schemas; on[Neon](https://www.getdot.ai/integrations/neon) you paste a connection string for a read-only role. Every query carries a comment naming the user, the workspace, what triggered it and a link to the chat, so any query in your logs traces back to its conversation ([August 2026 changelog](https://www.getdot.ai/changelog/2026-08-01-answer-lineage) ).


**Dashboards (Dot Apps):** describe what you want to track and Dot builds an interactive dashboard with KPIs, charts, tables and filters to publish, share or embed ([March 2026 changelog](https://www.getdot.ai/changelog/2026-03-27-apps) ). Dashboards refresh on demand or on a schedule, go out by email, Slack or Teams, and re-run only the queries a changed filter touches. Apps are off by default while they roll out; an admin switches them on.


**Security:** Dot queries your database in place without copying data, its LLM providers run with zero data retention, and it is SOC 2 Type II and GDPR compliant, with SSO, role-based access and your database's own permissions and row-level security.


**Pricing:** Free: $0 with 300 one-time credits and full Pro features. Pro: $180 a month billed annually ($200 month-to-month) with 150 credits a month. Team: $720 a month billed annually ($800 month-to-month) with 800 credits a month. Enterprise is custom. Every plan has unlimited users; you pay for credits (usage), not seats.


**Limits:** Dot reads; it doesn't change data, so screens that edit records belong in Retool or Appsmith. It isn't a pixel-precise report designer, and questions and scheduled deliveries use credits.


[Connect Postgres and start free](https://app.getdot.ai/register) .


## Reporting on a production Postgres safely


The bigger risk is where the tool connects: a heavy query on the primary that serves your app, as a user that can write. Here is the setup we recommend, in order (our test used shorter timeouts than shown, to watch them fire).


### Send reports to a read replica, and know how replicas cancel queries


A streaming replica ("read replica" on the managed services) takes report load off the primary. The catch: when the primary vacuums away row versions that a long replica query still needs, the replica waits and then cancels the query. We opened a report transaction on the replica, deleted and vacuumed rows on the primary, and about 31 seconds after the vacuum the replica returned:


```text
ERROR:  canceling statement due to conflict with recovery
DETAIL:  User query might have needed to see row versions that must be removed.
```


The wait is` max_standby_streaming_delay` , 30 seconds by default (what our test instance reported). On a reporting-only replica you can raise it, and the replica falls further behind while it waits; or turn on` hot_standby_feedback` , and the primary keeps those rows longer, which can bloat busy tables ([hot standby docs](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/hot-standby.html) ). Routine cancellations are a sign to move analytics off Postgres (below).


### Create a read-only role


```text
-- A group role that can read, and nothing else
CREATE ROLE reporting_ro NOLOGIN;
GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE app TO reporting_ro;
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO reporting_ro;
GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO reporting_ro;


-- Tables the app creates later become readable too
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE app_owner IN SCHEMA public
GRANT SELECT ON TABLES TO reporting_ro;


-- One login per tool, so each shows up separately in pg_stat_activity
CREATE ROLE bi_tool LOGIN PASSWORD 'use-a-long-random-password'
IN ROLE reporting_ro CONNECTION LIMIT 10;
```


- ` ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` only covers tables created by the role you name (here` app_owner` , the role your migrations run as); in our test, a table` app_owner` created later was readable by` bi_tool` at once.
- From PostgreSQL 15, ordinary roles can't create tables in` public` (` bi_tool` 's` CREATE TABLE` failed with` permission denied for schema public` ). On databases created on older versions, run` REVOKE CREATE ON SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC;` yourself.
- On PostgreSQL 14 and later,` GRANT pg_read_all_data TO bi_tool;` is a one-line alternative that read every table and still got` permission denied` on` INSERT` in our test, but it also covers any table holding emails, tokens or password hashes.


### Expose views, not tables, for sensitive data


If tables hold personal data, grant reporting a schema of views that select only the columns reports need:


```text
CREATE SCHEMA reporting AUTHORIZATION app_owner;
CREATE VIEW reporting.orders AS
SELECT id, amount, status, created_at FROM public.orders;
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA reporting TO reporting_ro;
GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA reporting TO reporting_ro;
```


In our test, a role with only these grants could count rows in` reporting.orders` , got` permission denied for table orders` on` public.orders` , and couldn't see the customer email column.


### Put timeouts and limits on the role


```text
ALTER ROLE bi_tool SET statement_timeout = '60s';
ALTER ROLE bi_tool SET idle_in_transaction_session_timeout = '5min';
ALTER ROLE bi_tool SET default_transaction_read_only = on;
```


Settings apply from the next login. With a 2-second timeout in our test,` SELECT pg_sleep(3)` failed with` canceling statement due to statement timeout` . The idle-in-transaction timeout ends sessions that sit in an open transaction holding back vacuum, and the` CONNECTION LIMIT` keeps one busy dashboard from using up your connection slots.


### Don't treat read-only mode as a security control


` default_transaction_read_only` catches mistakes, but any session can switch it off. In our test,` bi_tool` ran` SET default_transaction_read_only = off;` and then an` UPDATE` , which failed only because of the grants (` permission denied for table orders` ). The grants are the boundary; the setting is a seatbelt.


### Keep the database off the public internet


Require SSL, and reach a private database through an SSH tunnel, a gateway or the tool's own agent. If a tool can only connect over a public IP, allowlist its published address ranges and nothing wider.


## When to move analytics off Postgres


Signs a replica and a read-only role are no longer enough:


- Reports routinely exceed your statement timeout, or replica cancellations happen every week.
- Questions need data that isn't in Postgres: billing, CRM, ad spend.
- You need history the app overwrites, such as old order statuses or deleted rows.
- Dashboards aggregate most of a large table on every load. Postgres reads whole rows even when a report needs two columns; columnar engines read only the columns used.


The usual next step is a cloud warehouse: replicate Postgres into BigQuery or another warehouse with an ELT or change-data-capture tool and report from there (tools and cost controls in[BigQuery dashboard tools](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/bigquery-dashboard-tools) ). For a small team, DuckDB's[Postgres extension](https://duckdb.org/docs/extensions/postgres) can attach a replica read-only and copy tables into a columnar DuckDB file, or into MotherDuck in the cloud ([Dot connects to MotherDuck](https://www.getdot.ai/integrations/motherduck) too):


```text
INSTALL postgres;
LOAD postgres;
ATTACH 'host=replica.internal dbname=app user=bi_tool' AS pg (TYPE postgres, READ_ONLY);
CREATE TABLE orders AS SELECT * FROM pg.public.orders;
```


## AI and MCP on Postgres


An MCP server gives an AI assistant such as Claude or Cursor a direct SQL connection to your database. Treat it like any other reporting client: its own login in` reporting_ro` , the same timeouts, pointed at the replica. Which servers are worth using is in our[Postgres MCP server guide](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/postgres-mcp-server) .


If the audience is leadership, decide what belongs on the page before you pick the tool; see how to build an executive dashboard.
